Winger Jimmy Snuggerud was placed on IR to make room for his return. McMichael was only placed on IR three days ago to allow St. Louis to add youngsters Adam Jiricek and Otto Stenberg to the roster. He’d been out since Nov. 19 with a lower-body injury, missing just three games. He had a top-six role on the wing alongside Stenberg and Mason McTavish today, but skated only 11:48 with a -1 rating and didn’t factor in on any of the Blues’ five goals. It continues what has been a mixed start to McMichael’s Blues tenure. Acquired from the Capitals this summer in the Jordan Kyrou deal, the 25-year-old also inked a six-year, $40.5MM contract despite a slight drop-off in production last year. Early returns suggest the length of commitment may have been premature. He’s shooting at only 9.4% and has been limited to three goals and 11 points in 22 outings. His -12 rating is the worst on the team, but he’s been on the receiving end of some awful puck luck. His 52.9% Corsi share at even strength is second on the team behind only Dylan Holloway ’s 53.1%. Perhaps a 40-to-50-point threat is where McMichael will spend his prime. The 2019 first-rounder showed some more potential with a career-best 26-goal, 57-point campaign for Washington in 2024-25, but he’s been a sub-10% finisher ever since and likely can’t be consistently relied upon for 25-plus goals moving forward. items.summary: The Maple Leafs originally selected Bilecki with the No. 60 overall pick in the 2026 NHL Draft.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The Toronto Maple Leafs have agreed to terms on a three-year, entry-level contract with defense prospect Alexander Bilecki. Bilecki, 18, leads all Kitchener Rangers defensemen with five goals and 28 points in 24 games to begin the 2026-27 OHL season. The Mississauga product won both the OHL championship and the Memorial Cup as a member of the Rangers in 2025-26. Dan Milstein, Bilecki’s agent, announced the news on his social media accounts on Friday afternoon, with the club confirming the signing shortly thereafter. The Maple Leafs originally selected the 6’2″ left-shot defender in the second round (No. 60 overall) of the 2026 NHL Draft. Bilecki currently serves as an alternate captain in Kitchener. As a 2008-born player, he will likely return to the OHL for the 2027-28 season before turning pro in Toronto’s development system in 2028-29; with his NHL contract, Bilecki is now ineligible to play in the NCAA. The Maple Leafs acquired the draft pick they used to select Bilecki from the Los Angeles Kings at the 2026 trade deadline in exchange for forward Scott Laughton. Bilecki was the second of 10 draft picks the Maple Leafs made in 2026 and is the second to sign his entry-level contract with the team, following first-overall pick Gavin McKenna. The Maple Leafs announced the Bilecki signing shortly after they wrapped up a 3-1 win over the Boston Bruins on Friday afternoon. Morgan Rielly scored his first two goals of the 2026-27 season in the victory, with McKenna helping set up a late insurance goal by Colton Sissons in the third period. items.summary: The Canadiens will be without Kaiden Guhle against the Golden Knights, adding to their defensive challenges with Mike Matheson already sidelined. Meanwhile, Ivan Demidov inches closer to a return as Montreal looks to get its struggling power play back on track and clean up its execution.
items.body: LAS VEGAS— Any hope that Kaiden Guhle would be available to play against the Vegas Golden Knights on Saturday was erased when the Montreal Canadiens announced on Friday that the defenceman was day-to-day with an upper-body injury. Guhle left almost halfway through Wednesday’s 6-0 loss in Colorado, seconds after being hit from behind and knocked into the boards by Avalanche captain Gabriel Landeskog. He did not return. “It’s a tough loss, a tough guy to replace,” said Canadiens captain Nick Suzuki, who knew that the absence of Mike Matheson had already had its impact on the team’s recent skid. The Canadiens have lost three consecutive games in regulation for the first time since last November and the absence of their most used player—Matheson—has been an undeniable factor in that. Now, without both Matheson and Guhle, rookies Adam Engstrom and David Reinbacher will get more runway while Arber Xhekaj and Alex Carrier will need to be relied on almost as much as Lane Hutson and Noah Dobson typically are. The latter has struggled mightily this season, saying after Wednesday’s tough game in Denver, “Obviously it hasn’t been good enough at times, and that’s on me, I’ve got to find a way.” Dobson is Montreal’s highest-paid defenceman, a former 70-point producer who’s scored at least 10 goals in each of the last five seasons but is stuck on zero through 26 games of this one. But the Canadiens aren’t concerned about Dobson filling the opposing net. They need him to be stalwart in helping to keep goals out of theirs in the absence of their best defensive defenceman. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Steven Ellis The Ontario Hockey League (OHL) has just handed out some pretty significant discipline to two of its players. In the 2024-25 season with Niagara, he registered 11 goals and 10 assists for 21 points in 68 games. Last season, he put up just four goals to go along with 12 assists for 16 points in 67 games. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” Video review determined that Vancouver’s Drew O’Connor impaired Dan Vladar’s ability to play his position in the crease prior to Ty Mueller’s goal. items.title: Blackhawks place Patrick Kane on IR with lower-body injury
items.body: CHICAGO — The injury-depleted Chicago Blackhawks placed veteran forward Patrick Kane on injured reserve with a lower-body injury before Friday's game against the Rangers and recalled forward Landon Slaggert from Rockford of the AHL. Kane's move to the IR, retroactive to Wednesday, means the NHL's all-time leading American-born scorer will miss at least seven days. Blackhawks coach Jeff Blashill said that in a “best-case scenario,” the 38-year-old might return at Nashville on Thursday. Chicago is already without star center Connor Bedard, sidelined for about four months after undergoing right shoulder surgery on Monday. Defenseman Bowen Byram is skating, but remains out with an upper-body injury and his return date remains unclear. He has played in just six games after being acquired from Buffalo in an offseason trade. Blashill said he didn't believe Kane, a nine-time All-Star in his 20th season and second tour with Chicago, would be out long term. But then he hedged. “But I don't want to say that without knowing for sure, but we didn't put him on the LTIR (long-term injured reserve),” Blashill said. “We anticipate this is something that can be managed and he could be back sooner than later.” Kane has two goals and 16 assists in 22 games this season. He returned to the Blackhawks, who drafted him first overall in 2007, in July after signing a two-year, $16 million contract. The 24-year-old Slaggert has four goals and six assists in 20 games for Rockford. He has played in 102 career NHL games with the Blackhawks over three seasons, recording six goals and 11 assists. items.title: Connor Brown’s third-period goal lifts Devils to comeback win over Flames
items.body: NEWARK, N.J. — Connor Brown scored the go-ahead goal off a scramble in front with 3:58 remaining to lead the New Jersey Devils to a come-from-behind 5-3 win over the Calgary Flames on Friday. After Brown’s eighth goal, New Jersey had to kill off a penalty to Jonas Siegenthaler with 2:22 to play to preserve the win. The Devils, who are 11-3 at home, had their NHL-leading 10th comeback victory. Luke Hughes scored twice, including an empty-netter with 11 seconds left, and Jack Hughes had a goal and three assists for a four-point game for the seventh time in his career for the Devils. Timo Meier also scored and Jake Allen stopped 26 shots. Matt Coronado, Zach Whitehead and Joel Hanley had goals for the Flames. Devin Cooley had 29 saves. Jack Hughes tied it at 3 as he was falling down near the crease at 12:25 of the third period on assists from Dougie Hamilton and Arseny Gritsyuk. The Flames erased a 2-1 deficit in the second period with goals from Coronato and Whitecloud to grab a 3-2 lead. New Jersey scored twice within 12 seconds at the start of the second period to go ahead 2-1. Luke Hughes scored his eighth goal of the season from Jack Hughes and Hamilton 56 seconds into the period, then Meier had a goal at 1:08. Calgary went up 1-0 on Hanley's second goal of the season in his 12th game. Yegor Sharangovich and Simon Nemec had the assists, with Nemec extending his points streak to a career-high six games. Nemec was traded to the Flames in June. He was drafted by the Devils with the second pick of the 2022 draft and skated in 155 games with New Jersey.

Sure enough he never did, ending his day after 5:50 as the B’s lost 3-1. In a video posted by the New England Sports Network, the Boston captain was seen rushing up ice only to be bothered and heading back to the bench after no contact occurred, limping down the tunnel to the dressing room. Always concerning when such an injury occurs without contact, the Czech has been one of the most durable stars across the league over the past several seasons. Missing just five regular season games since 2022-23, Pastrňák had a streak of three consecutive 82-game campaigns end one year ago with an undisclosed injury . items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images Tell me if you’ve heard this before. Chris Tanev is injured. During a Friday matinee matchup between the Toronto Maple Leafs and Boston Bruins , Maple Leafs defenseman Chris Tanev suffered a lower-body injury that forced him to leave the game early. Early in the second period, Tanev went back behind his net to retrieve the puck. After delivering a breakout pass, he took a hit from Bruins forward Marc Kastelic. The check didn’t seem all that ferocious, but Kastelic caught Tanev in a soft spot down low, leaving Tanev in distress. Play came to a halt as Tanev needed assistance coming off the ice. He went down to the Leafs’ dressing room and didn’t return to the game. He logged just 7:53 of ice time across 11 shifts. The 36-year-old has seemingly been on the injured list as much as he has actually dressed for the Maple Leafs during his tenure with the Original Six franchise. He already missed nine games due to an upper-body injury back in October, which came after playing just 11 games for the entirety of the 2025-26 campaign. The injury comes just a few days after the Toronto native potted his first goal of the season, scoring in a 4-2 win over the New York Islanders on Tuesday night. Tanev has just two points in 16 appearances this season, registering a plus/minus of -3 while averaging a little over 18 minutes of ice time per game. Tanev has never competed in every regular-season game in his NHL career. In 894 appearances, he has scored 37 goals and 212 points, with another 16 points in 73 Stanley Cup Playoff appearances. He’s in the third season of his six-year contract, which carries an AAV of $4.5 million with a full no-move clause.

items.summary:
The average NHL goalie has never been taller.
Goalies hit an average of 6-foot-3 for the first time in League history in 2024-25, and after the average dipped by one-tenth of an inch in 2025-26, are right back up to those lofty heights so far this season. That’s an increase
items.body: Statistical edge due in part to better adjustment against east-west offensive tactics Goalies hit an average of 6-foot-3 for the first time in League history in 2024-25, and after the average dipped by one-tenth of an inch in 2025-26, are right back up to those lofty heights so far this season. That’s an increase of 1.3 inches from 15 years ago, which probably isn’t a shock given the NHL push toward larger goalies who, in theory, take up more of the net. So, what has that rise meant for smaller goalies during the same period? Perhaps surprisingly, the number of goalies playing regularly at 6-foot-1 or shorter has remained somewhat steady during the same 15-year period. Already this season, 18 goalies listed at 6-foot-1 or shorter have appeared in at least one game, and 15 are playing a regular role, same as last season and one below the average across the previous four seasons. That list includes rookies Jacob Fowler of the Montreal Canadiens (6-1), Dylan Garand of the New York Rangers (6-1) and Devon Levi of the Edmonton Oilers (6-0). “Honestly, it's less of a conversation now than it used to be,” said Levi, adding size is not something he discusses with good friends and offseason training partners Garand and Jet Greaves of the Columbus Blue Jackets, a fellow 6-foot goalie. “The game has changed a lot in the past, I don't know, 10 years, and it continues to change, and there's so much more than just being big.” The gap between the number of games played by goalies 6-foot-1 or shorter and goalies 6-foot-5 or taller has shrunk significantly the past 15 years, from 856 games in 2011-12 to an average of 152.2 during the past five seasons, and smaller goalies had only played seven more games this season. items.summary: The Philadelphia Flyers have had a bounce-back stretch of hockey after a terrible start to the season. However, the team's defensive structure is holding them back.
items.body: David Kirouac-Imagn Images Adam Proteau Partner Nov 27, 2026 6:32 PM Published Nov 27, 2026 6:32 PM The Philadelphia Flyers have had a bounce-back stretch of hockey after a terrible start to the season. However, the team's defensive structure is holding them back. Despite a horrendous start to the season, the Philadelphia Flyers are slowly scratching and clawing their way to back relevancy in the Metropolitan Division. Since they stumbled out to a 5-10-5 record through their opening 20 games, the Flyers have gone 5-2-1, a mark that includes victories over the Ottawa Senators , Buffalo Sabres and Montreal Canadiens . Philadelphia also has benefitted from playing in a weaker division, where elsewhere, their poor start probably would've stamped their fate. If there's one thing that’s hurting Philly more than anything, it's their defense. The Flyers' 4.33 goals-against average (third-highest in the league in this recent stretch) has to be especially frustrating because the offense has finally come around, with their 3.83 goals-for average ranking seventh in the same span. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Rob Gray-Imagn Images Some roster management for the team in Orange County, as it trudges through the start of the holiday season without one of its star players. According to the NHL Media Site, the Anaheim Ducks have placed forward Leo Carlsson on injured reserve with an upper-body injury. Carlsson has been out of action since last Saturday, when he was hurt during a game against the Utah Mammoth . During that contest, Carlsson was attempting to get the puck into the offensive zone. He was met with a firm check from Mammoth defenseman Mikhail Sergachev, which led to the two colliding with a linesman at the Utah blue line. Carlsson sat on the ice for a few minutes, with his hands to his face, before being helped off the ice by the Ducks’ training staff. Anaheim went on to lose to the Mammoth, 3-2. The young Swede has already missed the past two contests, which saw the Ducks lose to the Seattle Kraken , before hammering the San Jose Sharks 7-0 on Wednesday night. With Carlsson’s placement on IR retroactive to Nov. 21, he will be forced to miss Anaheim’s home-and-home against the rival Los Angeles Kings , but will be eligible to return to the lineup next Tuesday, when the Ducks welcome the Minnesota Wild to town. After signing his massive new deal prior to the start of the 2026-27 season, the 21-year-old has been a key part of Anaheim’s success in the early going. In 24 appearances, Carlsson has scored seven goals and 22 assists for 29 points, sitting fourth on the team in goals and tied for second in points. items.body: Two weeks ago, the Federal Aviation Administration in the United States made a sudden decision to ground all planes, interrupting air travel across the country. This had the potential to throw the sports world into chaos too, as teams were making their way to their next locations. In the end, the schedule carried on as normal for the NHL. There were no game postponements and everyone got to where they needed to be. The NFL's games went on as planned too, but there was at least one element affected when officiating assignments had to be overhauled. Four NFL refs had to officiate two games on the same day. Starting with an afternoon Dolphins-Colts game in Indianapolis, the refs then had to drive to Cincinnati to be ready for an 8:20 p.m. ET start time for the Steelers-Bengals game. In the end, the nationwide grounding lasted a little over four hours and the sports world was not affected on a greater scale. But what if it went on longer and had a wider-ranging impact? items.title: Ukraine urges countries to follow Canada’s lead in barring Russian athletes
items.body: Ukraine's sports minister wants other countries to follow Canada's lead in blocking Russian teams from international hockey tournaments. Matviy Bidnyi, in an op-ed published Friday by the Ukrainian news agency RBC-Ukraine, credited diplomatic efforts by Ukrainian government officials for Canada's decision to bar Russian players from next month's world junior hockey championship in Edmonton and Red Deer, Alta. Bidnyi said he is pushing for similar restrictions in other countries to prevent Russia's return to international hockey. Prime Minister Mark Carney said earlier this month that Russian players would not be permitted to compete in Canada as long as Russia's war in Ukraine continues. The International Ice Hockey Federation announced Wednesday it would challenge a Court of Arbitration for Sport ruling ordering the reinstatement of Russian teams to five international championships. Russia and Belarus have been barred from international hockey since Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, and several European federations have vowed to boycott games if Russia is allowed to compete.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Brad Penner The New York Islanders announced Friday that forward Kyle Palmieri will be out six-to-eight months with a torn ACL and meniscus in his right knee. The team placed the winger on injured reserve earlier this week after he suffered what they termed as a lower-body injury against the Toronto Maple Leafs on Monday. It’s the same injury that Palmieri, 35, suffered almost one year ago to the day that forced him to miss the final 57 games of the 2025-26 regular season. If he misses the rest of the current season, he will have only played 48 games since the end of the 2024-25 campaign. Palmieri had four goals and five assists for nine points in 23 games this season. Through 17 NHL seasons, the 2009 first-round pick has 280 goals and 274 assists for 554 points in 948 regular-season games with the Islanders, New Jersey Devils and Anaheim Ducks . He’s twice hit the 30-goal mark and has recorded at least 50 points four times, which includes a career-high 57 in 2015-16 with the Devils. He’s also appeared in 68 career Stanley Cup Playoff games, where he’s recorded 18 goals and 14 assists for 32 points. He was part of the Ducks’ and Islanders’ conference final runs in 2015 and 2021, respectively. Palmieri, born in Smithtown, N.Y., and raised in New Jersey, spent parts of four seasons in the American Hockey League. He scored 75 goals and added 59 assists for 134 points in 148 career games. The Islanders go into Friday with a 12-7-5 record and 29 points , which puts them third in the Metropolitan Division .

Palmieri had logged four goals and five assists through 23 games in 2026-27 prior to his latest setback. His latest string of injury misfortune comes after the 17-year vet had built up a reputation as one of the game's more durable players — playing in at least 50 regular-season games in 12 of those seasons, including a streak of 223 consecutive appearances for the Islanders prior to his injury last year. "Playing 1,000 games going into last year, that was a goal of mine and to be able to accomplish that was great," he said. items.title: Kessel’s love of playing in NHL led to U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame
items.summary: The 2026 U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame induction is Nov. 30. This year's class includes Amanda Kessel, Phil Kessel, T.J. Oshie, Ryan Suter and Stan Wong. Here, NHL.com senior draft writer Mike Morreale profiles Phil Kessel.
items.body: 3-time Cup champ holds ironman streak with 1,064 straight regular-season games The 2026 U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame induction is Nov. 30. This year's class includes Amanda Kessel, Phil Kessel , T.J. Oshie , Ryan Suter and Stan Wong. Here, NHL.com senior draft writer Mike Morreale profiles Phil Kessel. Phil Kessel played through the pain, the bumps, the bruises and all those mornings when he arrived at the rink just not feeling right. He’d play 1,064 consecutive regular-season games, in fact, an NHL Ironman record built over nearly 13 years and five teams. He played through injuries others never knew about, the pressure of being a star and three long Stanley Cup Playoffs runs. Kessel never set out to chase the record. In an interview with NHL Network Radio and during his election press conference, he said he simply hated sitting out. "I don't think it was ever a priority," Kessel said. "I just always wanted to play in the games. I love playing the games. I love playing hockey and I never wanted to miss. "As a player and competitor, you never want to sit out. You never want to be in the stands. You never want to be injured. You always want to be out there." That passion, durability and understated competitiveness helped make Kessel one of the most accomplished American players of his generation. Now, the reluctant superstar and three-time Stanley Cup champion is headed to the U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame. Kessel and his sister, Amanda, an Olympic gold medalist and four-time IIHF Women's World Championship gold medalist, headline the Class of 2026 to be inducted at the dinner and ceremony at the Grand Hyatt Washington in Washington, D.C., on Nov. 30. The Madison, Wisconsin, natives will become the second sister-brother combination inducted, joining Cammi Granato and Tony Granato.

Petry was a second-round pick by Edmonton back in 2006, going 45th overall. Four years later, he made the jump to the NHL and by the 2011-12 season, he was a full-fledged regular with the Oilers. items.body: PHILADELPHIA – A classic nor-easter storm barrelled into Philadelphia Thursday afternoon for U.S. Thanksgiving, lashing semi-deserted streets with sheets of rain driven sideways by winds gusting up to 80 kilometres per hour. Practising inside a giant hockey arena staffed, it seemed, by a security guard and the Zamboni driver, the Canucks were sheltered from a storm that felt somehow familiar because the National Hockey League’s worst team has been buffeted by severe wind and rain all season. The rebuilding Canucks play Game 28, completing the first third of their season, Friday against the Philadelphia Flyers. Vancouver has six wins. And its 20 regulation losses are five more than the next worst team in the standings, the Pittsburgh Penguins. The volatile weather, of course, was forecast as soon as the Canucks were tipped into the franchise’s first full-scale rebuild this century by the Quinn Hughes trade 11½ months ago. But for all the projected problems, effort was not supposed to be one of them. items.title: Brenden Dillon Receives Four-Game Suspension
items.summary: New Jersey Devils defenseman Brenden Dillon has received a four-game suspension for an illegal check to the head on Denton Mateychuk.
items.body: Register Login Brenden Dillon Receives Four-Game Suspension By Brian La Rose | at November 26, 2026 6:00 pm With the Devils having an early afternoon game on Friday, the Department of Player Safety was going to have to make a quick ruling on the fate of Brenden Dillon after his hearing today. They did just that, announcing that the defenseman has received a four-game suspension for his hit on Columbus blueliner Denton Mateychuk . In the video accompanying the announcement, it was noted that Dillon was deemed to have elevated “upward and unnecessarily and making Mateychuk’s head the main point of contact on a hit where such head contact was avoidable” . Because it was deemed avoidable, it became grounds for suspension under Rule 48. Meanwhile, he received a match penalty for the hit, which occurred a little past the midway mark of the first period. It is the second suspension of the 36-year-old’s career, the other coming back in February 2024, also for an illegal check to the head. However, since more than two years had elapsed, he didn’t qualify as a repeat offender for the purpose of salary forfeiture, though the prior act could still be considered when determining the number of games of the suspension. Dillon will forfeit a little over $82K in salary, with that money going to the Players’ Emergency Assistance Fund. Meanwhile, he’ll be eligible to return on December 5th against Pittsburgh. Vladislav Kolyachonok , who scored in his Devils debut two weeks ago, has been serving as the seventh defenseman since then and should draw back into the lineup while Dillon is serving his suspension. Late and at the head. Definitely altered Denton’s life. We should’ve left Dillon as a healthy scratch.

items.title: Why Maple Leafs’ William Nylander is getting a power-play demotion
items.summary: Hiller has removed Nylander from the flank of the club’s top power-play unit, a position the elite offensive talent has essentially owned throughout his prime.
items.body: BOSTON — In the ongoing discussion of William Nylander ’s underwhelming performance this month, Jim Hiller once said that there are “different ways” to hold players accountable for poor play. The head coach of the Toronto Maple Leafs did not bench his superstar winger for so much as a shift after Nylander’s direct giveaway to Matthew Knies ended up costing his reeling team a win at home Saturday. But Hiller has removed Nylander from the flank of the club’s top power-play unit, a position the elite offensive talent has essentially owned throughout his prime. A shocking sight, to be sure, at Boston’s TD Garden Thursday, as Nylander took reps with the seldom-used second unit and Kirill Marchenko joined PP1. In the past, it would’ve been Gavin McKenna or, perhaps, John Tavares getting the PP2 bump. “I think it was supposed to happen last game, but I didn't really pick up on it,” said Nylander, interpreting his demotion as punishment for his mistake against Columbus. “So, we’ll see how long he keeps it like that for. Amid his slump, Nylander is also skating on Toronto’s third line, now centred by Marlies call-up Aatu Räty and flanked by energy bug Easton Cowan. Räty is generally used in the defensive zone, so expect Hiller to get Nylander some extra O-zone starts with other linemates. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: David Kirouac-Imagn Images The Montreal Canadiens suffered a 6-0 defeat at the hands of the Colorado Avalanche on Wednesday, but the total loss for Canadiens winger Florian Xhekaj, specifically, is just a bit larger. On Thursday, the NHL Department of Player Safety announced that they have fined Xhekaj $2,426.98, the maximum allowable amount under the collective bargaining agreement (CBA), for his trip of Avalanche forward Fedor Svechkov during Wednesday’s game. The play in question occurred late in the third period when Svechkov had the puck in the Colorado zone, and Xhekaj checked him from the side while kicking out his right leg from behind and throwing him down in a clear and obvious slewfoot. Xhekaj, who has a goal and two assists for three points in 12 games this season, was assessed a match penalty and ejected from the game for the play. This came shortly after defenseman Arber Xhekaj, Florian’s brother, checked Avalanche defenseman Brent Burns from behind at the Colorado blueline, causing Burns to get up slowly from the ice while a giant scrum formed as multiple Avalanche players came to Burns’ defense. Burns would require stitches after the play, but is expected to be fine. It was a rowdy affair on Wednesday, even if the score was not competitive. There was a total of 57 penalty minutes assessed in the game, with the Xhekaj brothers accounting for 33 of them. This is the 22-year-old Florian Xhejak’s first instance of league-levied discipline. Arber Xhekaj, on the other hand, has been fined by the NHL on three seperate occasions. The Athletic’s Peter Baugh reported that forward Gabriel Perreault is expected to miss the next four to six weeks with a lower-body injury. Perreault, 21, is in his second full season with the Rangers. Last year, his rookie season, the former first-round pick scored 12 goals and 27 points in 49 games with a net-zero rating, while averaging 15:59 of ice time per game. Still, he had a relatively slow start to the campaign. 19 of his 27 points came after the calendar flipped to March. This season, Perreault is again averaging approximately one point every two games. Before the injury, the middle-six winger registered seven goals and 11 points in 24 games with a -2 rating, averaging 16:39 of ice time per game. However, it was a reverse pace from last year. Perreault scored seven points in October, but only has four in November. Regardless, even if he isn’t New York’s leading offensive talent, he is a big part of the team’s future. Given his recovery timeline, he won’t return to the lineup until Christmas, at the earliest. Meanwhile, Pärssinen has the opportunity to play in his first NHL contest since last season. items.body: New Jersey Devils defenceman Brenden Dillon received a four-game suspension on Thursday for an illegal hit to the head of Columbus Blue Jackets defenceman Denton Mateychuk. Dillon was assessed a match penalty for the check during the first period of the Devils' shootout win in Columbus on Wednesday night. Mateychuk left the game after the hit. Dillon forfeits $82,474.24 based on his average annual salary and under the terms of the collective bargaining agreement. The money goes to the Players’ Emergency Assistance Fund. On the play, Mateychuk skated through neutral ice and entered the zone before moving the puck to a teammate. Once the puck was gone, Dillon finished a “high, hard check, elevating upward and unnecessarily and making Mateychuk's head the main point of contact on a hit where such head contact was avoidable,” the NHL's department of player safety said in a video. Blue Jackets coach Rick Bowness said after the game: "I’ve coached Dillon. He’s not a dirty player. He’s a hard player. He caught him in a bad spot, and that’s a bad hit. It is.” Bowness said Wednesday that he spoke with Mateychuk and the defenceman “feels fine.” Bowness added that “protocol will take over and we’ll go from there.”

He doesn’t want to revisit the frustrations, rehash the circumstances that led to his departure from New Jersey, or turn Friday’s return to the Devils into some sort of referendum on who was right and who was wrong. And with a five-game point streak in his back pocket, the Calgary Flames defenceman has some pretty good evidence that the change of scenery he needed is paying off. “It's probably a better spot for me,” Nemec said of his new team. “I just feel better here, and I got more room to play, more room to grow, and that's what I wanted. “I'm thankful for what happened in New Jersey. But the bigger story is what has happened since Nemec landed in Calgary. items.title: Even after missing out on Dylan Larkin, the Minnesota Wild should remain all-in
items.summary: The Wild can ill afford to waste what might be their final year with Quinn Hughes.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Nick Wosika-Imagn Images The Minnesota Wild are in a tough spot. Just under a year after mortgaging a sizeable chunk of their future to land star defenseman Quinn Hughes from the Vancouver Canucks , the Wild seem no closer to signing the 27-year-old to a new contract. If anything, Wild general manager Bill Guerin sounds less and less confident each time he’s asked about the situation. And yet … from a hockey standpoint, the Wild haven’t given Hughes any reason not to sign with them. As of Thursday, they’re tied with the Carolina Hurricanes atop the NHL standings with 41 points. They’ve won 18 of 27 games this season, along with just four regulation losses. Right now, they have to be the odds-on favorites to come out of the Western Conference. Hughes has missed Minnesota’s last three games with an undisclosed injury, but it shouldn’t be long before he returns to the lineup — and when he’s played, the Wild have given him more freedom than ever. The 5’10” righty has already amassed 34 points (eight goals, 26 assists) in 24 games this season, good for second on the Wild in scoring. He’s also averaging a career-high 27:49 of ice time per game. When healthy, Hughes is right there with Cale Makar in the Norris Trophy race every single year, and Hughes will likely continue to be the standard against which all undersized puck-moving defense prospects are measured until the day he retires. He’s as elusive and dangerous as any player in the league. The Wild have a ton of money coming off the books after this season, and you can bet they’d love nothing more than to give most of it to Hughes. Guerin and Wild owner Craig Leipold already made a big statement last year by making Kirill Kaprizov the highest-paid player in the game, at least for a moment.

items.summary: The fisticuffs at center ice between Tyrel Bauer and Tanner Jeannot brought back some old-time hockey vibes at TD Garden.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Fighting might not be as popular as it once was in the NHL, but the 2026-27 season has delivered plenty of highlight-reel, viral fisticuffs through the first quarter and beyond, up to U.S. Thanksgiving. On Wednesday night, Winnipeg Jets defenseman Tyrel Bauer and Boston Bruins winger Tanner Jeannot offered one of the season’s best bouts, dropping the gloves for an over-minute fight at center ice at Boston’s TD Garden. The Jets went on to win 4-2, but it wasn’t the result that most will remember from this game. On Thursday’s episode of Daily Faceoff LIVE , co-hosts Tyler Yaremchuk and Carter Hutton dove into the fight that took sports headlines on U.S. Thanksgiving eve. Tyler Yaremchuk: Was this the fight of the year last night? This is some good old-school hockey here. It’s Tyrel Bauer and Tanner Jeannot at center ice at TD Garden; I love the look of this with the big B in the middle. This was just again. This is almost like what you would see every second night when you played in the AHL. Carter Hutton: Yeah, this was it, man. I remember living with Brandon Bollig, who was our fighter with the Rockford IceHogs, and I would complain about my hips being sore from playing too often. Meanwhile, he’s icing his knuckles and fighting every single night. This was a heavyweight bout, man. These guys stood at center ice at TD Garden and absolutely threw. Early in the fight, Bauer gets him and spins him around. For Jeannot to come back with that quick spin and regrip and then throw it at him is world-class, man. This is a great fight. items.title: Checking in on the NHL playoff picture at U.S. Thanksgiving
items.summary: American Thanksgiving has long served as an unofficial measuring stick to gauge teams’ likelihood of making the playoffs. Emily Sadler evaluates the NHL’s post-season picture.
items.body: It’s American Thanksgiving. Do you know where your NHL team is? The U.S. holiday has long served as an unofficial measuring stick to gauge teams’ likelihood of making the playoffs. Put simply, clubs sitting in playoff position at this time of year have a roughly 75 per cent chance of remaining there by season’s end. While far from a perfect rule, it’s generally pretty accurate. Take the past two seasons, for example — of the 16 teams inside the playoff window at Thanksgiving in back-to-back years, 12 ultimately clinched a spot. The rate was higher in 2022-23 and 2023-24, with 13 sitting and staying in a playoff spot. To round out our five-year sample size of recent examples, the 2021-22 campaign also showed a 75 per cent clinch rate of teams in playoff position at the U.S. Thanksgiving mark. When we think about noteworthy exceptions to this benchmark, the 2018-19 St. Louis Blues always jump to mind. By Thanksgiving of that season, the team was sitting last in the Central, lagging seven points behind the Dallas Stars for the second wild card spot, and had just made a coaching change by firing Mike Yeo and promoting Craig Berube in his place. (Of course, what made that squad particularly special was the fact they remained in last place early into the new calendar year, not launching their dramatic and historic comeback until January.) While the Blues are the most extreme case, the past five years show some interesting instances, too — just look at last year’s standings. The 2025-26 Buffalo Sabres brought us the closest thing to those 2018 Blues, sitting last in the Eastern Conference by November’s end, five points outside of the final wild card spot. items.summary: While Kirill Marchenko won't solve all of the Toronto Maple Leafs' problems, bringing him back will certainly give the team an offensive boost when they need it most.
items.body: Nick Turchiaro-Imagn Images Adam Proteau Partner Nov 26, 2026 5:11 PM Published Nov 26, 2026 5:11 PM While Kirill Marchenko won't solve all of the Toronto Maple Leafs' problems, bringing him back will certainly give the team an offensive boost when they need it most. Toronto Maple Leafs winger Kirill Marchenko has had a roller-coaster start to the season. The 26-year-old found himself in a new jersey just one day before the 2026-27 regular season began after he was dealt by the Columbus Blue Jackets . Then he signed a massive $75-million extension before even finding a place to live in Toronto. After finding immediate success with his new club (six goals and 14 points in 14 games), he was sidelined for 12 games with a lower-body injury. His new team proceeded to go 2-9-1 in his absence. The good news for the Maple Leafs is that Marchenko is back and ready to play Friday, against the Boston Bruins . But let's be clear: he's not going to magically make the Buds into a winning machine. Good teams don't go 1-9-0 because they've been without one injured star player. The Colorado Avalanche were fine without Cale Makar and continue to win without Nathan MacKinnon. The Montreal Canadiens have been without Ivan Demidov, Mike Matheson, and multiple other players at different points through the start of the season and find ways to churn out victories. That said, the Maple Leafs definitely will benefit from Marchenko's return. We're talking about an elite skater who's 6-foot-3, is producing at a point-per-game pace and a first-line force. By Ryan Long | at November 26, 2026 9:39 am A fight between two willing players, or a response to a dirty hit, is part of how hockey polices itself and part of what makes it special. But something has changed in how players react to legal hits. The old approach was to spring into action after an egregious or illegal hit and, after a big clean hit on a teammate, remember the number and settle it later. Now the reflex is to go after the hitter the moment the whistle blows, often halfheartedly, whether the hit was clean or not. So have fights and scrums after clean hits become an issue? The numbers say they have, and the league has had a tool to deal with them for more than three decades. A Pro Hockey Rumors review of NHL play-by-play data from all 399 regular-season games through Nov. 25 found 110 fights. Forty-three of them, or 39.1%, came within 10 seconds of a hit that drew no penalty, with no faceoff in between. In 32 of those 43 fights, one of the combatants was the player who delivered the hit. The instigator penalty was called seven times in those 43 fights. Only eight instigator penalties have been called league-wide this season. In 28 of the 43, the responding team received no penalty beyond the matching fighting majors. The fights are only part of it. Another 60 unpenalized hits this season were followed by roughing calls but no fight. That’s 1.4 of those scrums for every fight after a legal hit, and none of them show up in fight totals. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources American Thanksgiving represents a fascinating point in the NHL season because the sample sizes are large enough to matter for struggling teams, yet the season is just young enough that it’s still possible to save it in rare cases. The most famous example: the 2018-19 St. Louis Blues, who named Craig Berube interim head coach in November and rose from dead last in the NHL standings as late as Jan. 2 to winning the Stanley Cup. Maybe a case study like that gives teams false hope, maybe not. But we do frequently see firings start to pop up around this time of year in the NHL. In 2023-24, we saw four head coach firings before the league reached its late-December holiday break. The 2024-25 season had four bench bosses axed between Nov. 19 and Dec. 26 alone. The first pink slip of 2025-26 came in mid-January. Recent history thus tells us it’s not too soon to run a temperature check of every seat in the league. items.body: Register Login Brenden Dillon To Have Hearing For Hit On Denton Mateychuk By Ryan Long | at November 26, 2026 8:31 am Devils defenseman Brenden Dillon will have a hearing with the NHL Department of Player Safety today for an illegal check to the head/interference on Blue Jackets defenseman Denton Mateychuk , the league announced . The league hasn’t said whether the hearing will be by phone or in person. A phone hearing would cap any suspension at five games, while an in-person hearing would allow for a longer one. The hit came at 12:54 of the first period of New Jersey’s 3-2 shootout win in Columbus last night. Dillon caught Mateychuk in the Devils’ defensive zone and got a five-minute major and a match penalty. That ended his night after four shifts and 3:23 of ice time. Mateychuk went down hard and did not return. Columbus head coach Rick Bowness said afterward that the former 12th overall pick was fine and that concussion protocol would take over. New Jersey killed off the major and won on Arseny Gritsyuk ’s shootout goal, improving to 17-8-0 on the season. Dillon has been here before. In February 2024, while with the Jets, he was suspended three games and forfeited nearly $61K in salary for an illegal check to the head of Penguins forward Noel Acciari , which also drew a match penalty. Last November, he was fined $5K, the maximum allowable under the CBA, for boarding Blackhawks forward Tyler Bertuzzi . He also served a one-game suspension with the Sharks in December 2017 for slashing Capitals defenseman Madison Bowey . Because more than 18 months have passed since his last suspension, Dillon isn’t considered a repeat offender under the CBA, which affects only how much salary he’d forfeit. items.title: Canadiens’ Florian Xhekaj receives match penalty for slew foot
items.body: It was a chippy affair between the Montreal Canadiens and Colorado Avalanche on Wednesday night, and Florian Xhekaj was right in the middle of all of it. It culminated late in the third period, when the forward was handed a match penalty for slew-footing Avalanche forward Fedor Svechkov, subsequently ending his night. The infraction happened with just over a minute remaining in the game as the Canadiens were down 6-0. The whistle had just sounded when Xhekaj tripped up Svechkov and was assessed an intent-to-injure penalty. That would be five of Xhekaj's 22 penalty minutes on the evening, as he was also assessed a 10-minute misconduct in the second period. A match penalty comes with an automatic ejection and review from the league. Florian wouldn't be the only Xhekaj to amass a fair few PIMs on Wednesday, as brother Arber — a Canadiens defenceman — wracked up 16 of his own. The brothers combined for 33 of the 42 total penalty minutes in this game. Avalanche captain Gabriel Landeskog wasn't thrilled with the antics of the Xhekaj brothers, telling reporters that they "have to use (their) head a little bit." "The Xhekaj brothers, they wanted to get involved so we'll see what's going to happen with that," Landeskog told reporters after the game . "I think for one of the most storied franchises and one of the most respected franchises in all of hockey, and you've got two guys doing that." Florian, who has played 17 career NHL games, has 54 penalty minutes. There will be no chance for revenge, though, on either side as Wednesday's match wrapped up the season series between the two inter-conference teams.

The Department announced that Dillon will have a hearing on Thursday for an illegal check to the head and interference against Columbus Blue Jackets defenceman Denton Mateychuk in their game Wednesday. items.body: Canadiens icon scored 544 goals with C.C.M. three-piece twig that helped 'revolutionize' game Maurice “Rocket” Richard is sitting in the Montreal Canadiens dressing room during the 1959-60 season, the last of his illustrious NHL career. The smiling superstar is turning revolutions of black friction tape over the thick blade of his heavy wood stick for team photographer David Bier. It is a ritual the greatest goal-scorer of his generation had done many hundreds of times; on this occasion, his sons Maurice Jr. and Normand are witness to it in the Montreal Forum dressing room. This classic photo was published as part of a six-page Oct. 29, 1960 “Perspectives” newspaper supplement retrospective written by Le Soleil editor Guy Fournier, the Rocket having announced his retirement six weeks earlier. He had served as captain his final four seasons, winning the Stanley Cup in each of them, his eighth career championship having come in 1960. A 1942 newspaper advertisement for C.C.M. sticks, and Maurice Richard in front of a Montreal Forum stick rack, having just been named captain of the Canadiens for the 1956-57 season. One of the intriguing things about this snapshot of history -- apart from Rocket’s battered knuckles -- is the stamp on the wide, flat blade the Canadiens icon is about to cover with tape. It reads: “PATTERN MADE BY … EXTRA SPECIAL,” with C.C.M. stick-maker Ernie Evernden’s signature between the capital letters. This Wisconsin rock elm stick, very popular in the day, was a C.C.M. Pattern-Made Professional from the stock at long-ago Raymond Hardware, a regular Canadiens supplier, located about 3 miles from the Forum. items.body: ST. PAUL, Minn. — Logan Cooley and Dylan Guenther each had a goal and an assist for the Utah Mammoth , in a 4-3 win on Wednesday night that gave the Minnesota Wild their first regulation loss in 16 games. Blake Coleman had two goals and Bobby Brink also scored for the Western Conference-leading Wild (18-4-5), who were a franchise-best 12-0-3 in their previous 15 games. After Coleman cut the deficit to one with 4:04 left, Mammoth center Barret Hayton was whistled 19 seconds later for a double-minor penalty for high-sticking Joel Eriksson Ek. The Wild had a power play for the remainder of regulation but managed only two shots. Karel Vejmelka made 22 saves for his first win in seven starts since Oct. 24 and Lawson Crouse and Dmitri Simashev scored for the Mammoth, whose second-period leads of 3-1 and 4-2 gave the Wild a two-goal deficit for the first time since their last regulation loss at Calgary on Oct. 22. Crouse’s tip-in of Vincent Trocheck’s shot in the first period stopped Minnesota’s scoring-first streak at 15 straight games. That was tied for the second-longest run in NHL history and best in the league since Montreal in 1972. The Canadiens have the record with 18 consecutive games, set during the 1959-60 season. Kirill Kaprizov’s franchise-record streak of 15 straight games with a point ended, as did his run of six consecutive games with multiple assists. That was the second-longest streak in NHL history, behind Wayne Gretzky's eight in 1984. Kaprizov went without a point for just the third time in 27 games, with linemates Eriksson Ek and Matt Boldy also producing at a prolific rate this season. items.title: Ducks’ Cutter Gauthier becomes first American to score 21 goals in 14 games
items.body: Only three full seasons into his NHL career, Cutter Gauthier is rewriting record books. The Anaheim Ducks star forward has been on a near-unparalleled scoring surge in recent weeks, and after yet another goal against the San Jose Sharks on Wednesday night, he hit a mark last reached by Mario Lemieux more than three decades ago. With his 21st goal in the last 14 games, Gauthier became the first player to accomplish the feat since Lemieux in the 1992-93 season, and became the only American in NHL history to do so. He hit the mark with just under five minutes left in the first period against the Sharks, finishing off a power-play marker set up by Jackson LaCombe and Mikael Granlund to give his side a 3-0 lead. The only other players to score 21 in 14 games are Lemieux (1992-93 and 1988-89), Teeme Selanne (1992-93), Alexander Mogilny (1992-93), Bernie Nichols (1988-89) and Wayne Gretzky (1980-81, 1981-82, and 1983-84). Gauthier's run started on Oct. 29, when he potted two goals against the Buffalo Sabres. He went on to score back-to-back hat tricks against the Ottawa Senators and Vancouver Canucks, then grabbed two more against the Pittsburgh Penguins and St. Louis Blues over the course of his streak. With the majority of his goals — 19 of them — coming since the calendar turned to November, he may set the record for most goals in a calendar month in the coming days, with Selanne atop the ladder with 20. Gauthier is only the eighth player and second American to score 19 in a calendar month, and has two more games against the Los Angeles Kings on Nov. 27 and 28 to break the record. On the season, the 22-year-old has 23 goals — tied for the league lead with Leon Draisaitl of the Edmonton Oilers — and nine assists in 25 games.

It looks like the forward could miss some time, as post-game head coach Jon Cooper told reporters, including Manager of Media Relations Benjamin Pierce that he was “a little worried” and that he might be out for “a bit”. It’s not immediately clear where the injury happened but he exited during the second period, ending his night after just 6:34 on the ice. In a contract year the 27-year-old has stepped up in a big way, already at 13 points in 24 games when his career high is 22. Known to be a dependable shutdown winger, Holmberg has shown new elements to his game, being rewarded with time on the power play as well as a top six deployment, including tonight on Brayden Point ’s wing. Going 7-4-0 since star Nikita Kucherov ’s unexpected and league-shaking trade request , the Bolts lost to Carolina tonight and haven’t had the smoothest past few days. Last Sunday the superstar was benched in a convincing loss to Buffalo. Through it all, Holmberg has stayed in Cooper’s good graces, earning more shifts that night and continuing to cement himself as a vital middle-six role player. items.title: Canucks fall to Red Wings as Finnie, Arvidsson have three points each
items.body: DETROIT — Emmitt Finnie scored two early goals to lead the Detroit Red Wings to a 5-1 victory over the Vancouver Canucks on Wednesday night in a battle of last-place teams. Finnie added an assist and Viktor Arvidsson had a goal and two assists for Detroit, which had lost seven of eight. Lucas Raymond and J.T. Compher also scored and Daniil Tarasov made 25 saves. Vancouver had won three of five since breaking a 1-16-1 skid. Finnie got his first at 1:16, tipping in Arvidsson's shot from the right wing, then made it 2-0 at 4:05 by knocking in the rebound of Marco Kasper's shot. Finnie was the first Red Wings player to score twice in the first five minutes of a game since Brett Hull had two in the first 3:56 of a 5-2 win over the St. Louis Blues on Jan. 26, 2002. Hull finished that game with five points — three goals and two assists. Raymond made it 3-0 with a power-play goal with 57 seconds left in the first. Moritz Seider fed him the puck at the right faceoff spot, and he beat a screened Merilainen for his 10th goal of the season. Compher got Detroit's fourth goal at 6:24 of the second period, tapping in Michael Brandsegg-Nygard's pass at the back post. Paul Cotter ruined Tarasov's shutout bid with a goal at 7:26 of the third, but Arvidsson restored the four-goal lead at 8:08. items.body: SUNRISE, Fla. — Brad Marchand and Aleksander Barkov returned to the Florida lineup in style, with Marchand getting three assists and Barkov scoring an empty-netter to help the Panthers beat the Ottawa Senators 5-3 on Wednesday night. Anton Lundell, Sam Bennett, Niko Mikkola and Eetu Luostarinen also had goals for Florida, which got both Marchand and Barkov back after each missed nearly two months with knee injuries suffered in the season's opening week. It was Barkov's first home game for Florida since the final game of the 2025 Stanley Cup Final. Jacob Markstrom stopped 25 shots. Dylan Cozens and Philip Tomasino had goals 41 seconds apart early in the second period for Ottawa, with Artem Zub and Jake Sanderson picking up assists on both as the Senators took a 2-1 lead. The rest of the game was all Florida, and Ottawa's nine-game point streak (7-0-2) came to an end. Michael Amadio scored with 51 seconds left for the Senators. Mikkola tied it for Florida midway through the second period and Marchand — stickhandling around a pair of Senators — set up Lundell for the goal that gave the Panthers a 3-2 lead going into the third. Bennett's goal with 10:43 left sealed it, beating Ottawa goalie Linus Ullmark from close range for a 4-2 lead. The play started with Florida goalie Jacob Markstrom coming way out of the net, nearly to the blue line, to send a loose puck to the right-wing boards. Marchand played it to Lundell, who set up Bennett. Ullmark entered the game as the NHL's leader this season with a 1.44 goals-against average and a .938 save percentage. The Panthers solved him, becoming the first team to score four on Ullmark this season. In his first 13 appearances this season, Ullmark allowed three goals only once — in a 4-3 overtime win over Colorado on Nov. 12.

items.summary: Morgan Barron scored the tie-breaking goal late in the second period, Nico Daws made 21 saves, and the Winnipeg Jets added to their surge with a 4-2 victory over the Boston Bruins on Wednesday night.
items.body: BOSTON — Morgan Barron scored the tie-breaking goal late in the second period, Nico Daws made 21 saves, and the Winnipeg Jets added to their surge with a 4-2 victory over the Boston Bruins on Wednesday night. Kyle Connor and Josh Morrissey each had a goal for Winnipeg, which won its fourth straight road game and improved to 9-1-1 in its last 11 overall. Mark Scheifele, the Jets' career goals leader, added an empty-netter for the 381st of his career. Morgan Geekie and Fraser Minten scored for the Bruins, who dropped the second of their season-high six-game homestand. Jeremy Swayman stopped 14 shots. Barron’s goal came with 2:07 left in the second when he poked the puck between Swayman’s pads to make it 3-2 after the goalie mishandled the rebound of Mario Ferraro’s shot. Boston’s Tanner Jeannot and Winnipeg’s Tyrel Bauer squared off in a lengthy fight midway into the opening period that featured numerous haymakers. Trailing in the second, Boston tied it at 2 when Minten, positioned directly in front of the net, tipped Mason Lohrei’s shot by Daws at 10:57. Morrissey’s slap shot from the slot beat Swayman and gave the Jets a 2-1 edge late in the opening period. Off since a 7-5 victory over Washington at home Saturday, the Bruins had tied it at 1 on Geekie’s power-play goal off a pretty pass across the front of the net by David Pastrnak at 6:11. Connor’s wrister from the left circle made it 1-0 just 65 seconds into the game. The Bruins won the first meeting between the teams in overtime on Oct. 2.

items.body: PITTSBURGH — Joel Farabee had a goal and an assist and the Calgary Flames beat the Pittsburgh Penguins 6-3 on Wednesday night. Zayne Parekh had an assist to pass Miles Zaharko for the fifth-most points by a Flames’ defenceman younger than 21. Evgeni Malkin passed Bryan Trottier for 19th-most points in NHL history with a power-play goal and an assist for Pittsburgh. Malkin, who missed the last two games because of an injury, had his 382nd multipoint game and tied Teemu Selanne for fourth among players born and trained outside of North America. Rickard Rakell also had a power-play goal and Tommy Novak also scored. The Penguins scored two home power-play goals for the first time since an Oct. 3 win against Montreal. Arturs Silovs stopped 20 shots for the Penguins, who lost their fifth straight. Pittsburgh, last in the Eastern Conference, has lost 10 of 12 overall. The Flames won their 64th straight game when scoring four or more goals. They’re one four-goal win from tying the New York Rangers’ 65-game run from 2011-14, the longest mark in NHL history.
